name: Vespertine 0.12.2
body:
**Vespertine now works properly in Light Mode, lets outputs without a volume control use Vespertine's volume, and keeps analyzing your library while you listen from a network share.**

### Volume
- **Volume for fixed-volume outputs.** HDMI, optical and line-out DACs have no volume of their own, so Vespertine used to leave them at full level. Click the FIXED badge in the bottom bar, or open the output's device panel, and turn on **Volume control in Vespertine** to set the level in the app. Each output remembers its own choice and level, and the switch in Settings stays the default for every other output. Below 100% the output is no longer bit-perfect, and the labels say so.

### File analysis
- **Analysis keeps going while a share plays.** With a song playing from a network share, analyzing a selection or the whole library stayed at 0 until the music stopped. Analysis now reads one share file at a time alongside the song, steps aside while a song starts or its buffer runs low, and runs at full speed once the playing song is fully copied to the local cache.

### Fixed
- **Light Mode.** With macOS set to Light Mode, the menu bar window showed dark text on its dark panel, and some popovers, alerts and menus didn't match the rest of the app. Vespertine now draws dark everywhere, whatever the system appearance. Thanks for the report in [#68](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/issues/68).

### Also new
- A small “Made with ❤️ in Boston” line on both About screens.

### Known issues
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.12.2.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.12.1
body:
**Vespertine now plays smoothly from slow network shares, analyzes big libraries faster with shares included, plays hi-res on small USB-C DACs at the highest rate they offer, and keeps the keyboard and multi-selections where you expect them.**

### Network shares
- **Smooth playback from slow shares.** On a share that isn't very fast, playback could stutter and stall every few seconds, and pause, skip and seek could take seconds to respond. Vespertine now decodes a song from a share several seconds ahead, so a slow read no longer interrupts what's already buffered, and pause, skip, seek and output changes apply right away.
- **Fewer interruptions.** If the share falls behind more than once in a short time, Vespertine waits for a bit more audio before resuming, so you get a few longer pauses instead of a stop every few seconds.
- **The song comes first.** Copying a song to the local cache now steps aside while that song's buffer is running low.
- **No more crackling.** Songs from a share mounted in the Finder and added as a regular folder now pause to buffer instead of crackling.

### File analysis
- **Network shares are included.** Analyze Library now covers songs on network shares too. It still pauses while music plays from a share, so playback goes first.
- **Faster on big libraries.** Local files and share files are analyzed side by side instead of one queue waiting on the other, and local analysis uses half of the Mac's cores.
- **Progress in the sidebar.** A running library analysis shows its progress in the sidebar wherever you are, with a Stop button.
- **Several songs at once.** Choosing Analyze with several songs selected analyzes all of them and keeps the selection.

### USB DACs
- **Hi-res isn't cut down to 44.1 kHz.** On a DAC whose top rate is below the music's, such as a 96 kHz USB-C adapter, 176.4 kHz, 352.8 kHz and DSD used to play at 44.1 kHz. They now play at the DAC's top rate, keeping everything it can reproduce. Vespertine still uses an exact divisor of the music's rate when that keeps at least half of the DAC's top rate, such as 176.4 kHz for 352.8 kHz music on a 192 kHz DAC.
- **Real names for USB DACs.** A DAC that calls itself just “Headphone”, such as the UGREEN CM450, now shows its product name in the device picker and the signal path.
- **Loopback test with a muted loopback device.** If the Vespertine Loopback device was muted or turned down, every case ended with “No signal reached the input”. The test now turns it up for the run and puts it back afterwards.

### Fixed
- **Pause responds at once.** Pausing a song that streams from a slow network share stopped the sound right away, but the button could keep showing pause for a long while, and pressing it again paused instead of resuming. The button now switches as soon as you press it, and a second press resumes. The media keys behave the same way.
- **Keyboard follows your click.** Clicking a song gives that list the keyboard, so the arrow keys, Return and ⌘A act on the songs instead of the sidebar. The selected row's text, tags and heart stay readable on the highlighted row.
- **Multi-selections hold.** A multi-selection no longer shrinks on its own when another page was open before. A plain click inside a multi-selection selects just that song, and double-click or Return plays the song you chose.
- **⌘A on a big library.** Selecting the whole library froze the window for several seconds while the inspector read every song's tags. That work now runs in the background.

### Known issues
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.12.1.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.12.0
body:
**Vespertine now plays DST-compressed DSDIFF files and the LPCM music on DVD-Video discs natively, keeps every track of EAC CUE sheets, and starts songs from a network share right away even while a library scan is running.**

### DST-compressed DSDIFF
- **Plays natively.** Compressed `.dff` files used to go to a decoder that couldn't read DST, so they failed with “Decoder not found”. They now go through the same lossless DST decoder that SACD images use, so DST DSDIFF plays as DSD over DoP bit for bit, with BIT-PERFECT shown as for a DSF file, or through the usual DSD → PCM conversion.
- **Damage fails clearly.** Vespertine checks every frame's bounds, the optional DSDIFF index and its CRCs. A damaged file reports an error instead of playing silence.
- **Library upgrade.** On the first launch, DSDIFF files the library already holds are read again, so their durations and formats are right. Track IDs, play counts and playlists are kept.
- **Checked on real files.** All 59 DST DSDIFF files in a real collection, with stereo, 5- and 6-channel areas, decoded to the same DSD as an independent reference.

### DVD-Video LPCM
- **Discs play straight from the image.** Add a DVD-Video image (`.iso`) or a folder holding `VIDEO_TS`, and its LPCM music appears as albums: one per title, one track per chapter. Nothing is mounted, extracted or written.
- **Supported formats.** 16-, 20- and 24-bit audio at 48 and 96 kHz, 1 to 8 channels, within DVD-Video's limits.
- **Exact timing.** Timing comes from the disc's 90 kHz time stamps, not its rounded chapter times. Seeks land on the exact sample, and tracks that share a VOB join without a gap.
- **Damaged navigation.** On discs with inconsistent navigation, the tracks are rebuilt from the disc's own navigation packs. Menus and short preview clips are left out.
- **Not supported.** DVD-Audio, including MLP and the `AUDIO_TS` folder, is not supported. A DVD-Audio disc says so and adds nothing. Encrypted (CSS) discs need a decrypted copy.
- **Checked on real discs.** A 26-track DVD image and a two-album `VIDEO_TS` folder decoded sample for sample like independent extractions.
- **Details:** [DVD-Video LPCM](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/blob/main/docs/DVD-VIDEO-LPCM.md).

### Network shares
- **Songs start right away during a scan.** While a library scan is reading a network share, a song from that share used to take up to 40 seconds to start or seek, and could stall. Now, while that song is starting, seeking or playing from the share, the scan steps back to one request at a time so the song's reads go first. The scan still finishes, and goes back to full speed once the song plays from its local copy or stops.

### Fixed
- **CUE sheets from EAC.** When a CUE sheet named its audio file after a track's `TRACK` or `INDEX 00` line, the track could be lost or given to the wrong file. Each track now belongs to the file that holds its `INDEX 01`, pregap included.
- **Sidebar at launch.** Opening a library no longer briefly shows the empty-library screen, or makes the sidebar fill in row by row. The playlists and sources are there from the first frame, which also removes an AppKit warning that would become a crash in a future macOS.

### Known issues
- DVD-Video tracks are named “Track N”, because the format has no song titles. Rename them in the tag editor.
- Only the first LPCM stream of a DVD title plays. 20- and 24-bit DVD audio with 3 or more channels hasn't been checked on a real disc yet.
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.12.0.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID (Alexander Szeremeta, `7WMQ9ZV6V8`), notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.11.3
body:
**With exclusive access, Vespertine no longer changes the volume of the Mac's other sound output unless you ask it to, and the loopback test and 16-bit setting are now translated into every language.**

### Volume keys with exclusive access
- **Off by default.** While Vespertine holds a DAC exclusively, macOS moves the Mac's sound output to another device, often the built-in speakers. Vespertine used to copy the DAC's volume onto that output so the volume keys kept working, which meant other apps' sounds could play from the speakers at the DAC's level. Now it leaves that output's volume alone.
- **Your choice.** **Settings › Playback › Output › Volume keys control the device held exclusively** brings the old behaviour back: the volume keys, Control Center and the AirPods Max Digital Crown change the DAC's volume by way of the other output. Turning it off gives that output its own volume back at once. The setup assistant's "Volume keys follow Vespertine" switch sets it while exclusive access is on.
- **Clearer descriptions.** Settings, the output menu and the setup assistant now say what the volume keys do in each case.

### Translations
- **The loopback test is translated** in all 44 languages: the window, its menu item, the quick and full runs, the verdicts and Copy Report, and the loopback lines in the signal path.
- **So are Match 16-bit sources** and its explanation, and the new volume setting.

### Fixed
- **Long labels fit.** German "Abweichend" and the other languages' "Mixed" in the tag editor's disc and track fields, Brazilian Portuguese "Adicionadas Recentemente" in the sidebar, and long custom tag names such as MUSICBRAINZ_ALBUMARTISTID are no longer cut off.
- **Tag editor wording.** With only CUE or SACD disc-image tracks selected, the tag editor says the tags are saved in Vespertine's library instead of "Writes tags to 0 files".

### Known issues
- A stray icon can appear next to the sidebar button while the search field is active.
- Some long translations of "Recently Added" can still be cut off when the sidebar is at its narrowest.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.11.3.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID (Alexander Szeremeta, `7WMQ9ZV6V8`), notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.11.2
body:
**Vespertine now speaks 44 languages, welcomes new users with a setup assistant, remembers the output you chose, starts DSD CUE tracks at once, and can check its own signal path bit for bit with a loopback test.**

### 44 languages
- **Translated throughout.** The app, its menus, settings, error messages and VoiceOver labels are available in Amharic, Arabic, Bengali, Chinese (Simplified, Traditional for Taiwan, Traditional for Hong Kong), Czech, Danish, Dutch, Filipino, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Gujarati, Hausa, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Kannada, Korean, Malay, Malayalam, Marathi, Norwegian Bokmål, Persian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Punjabi, Romanian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu and Vietnamese. Vespertine follows the language set for it in System Settings.
- **Written for each language.** Counts use each language's plural forms, numbers use local decimal separators, and sentences are translated whole instead of being assembled from fragments.
- **Right to left.** Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu lay out right to left. The transport controls and seek bar stay left to right, as in Apple's own apps.
- **Readable scripts.** Letter spacing and the monospaced face are turned off for Arabic, Indic and Thai scripts, where they pull letters apart.
- **Any library, any language.** Analysis summaries and the starter smart playlists are translated when shown, so a library made in one language reads correctly in another.
- **No Russian.** Vespertine has no Russian localization, and the release build removes the one Sparkle bundles.
- The translations are careful machine translations, checked on screen but not yet reviewed by native speakers. Corrections are very welcome: please [open an issue](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/issues/new/choose).

### Setup assistant
- **A guided first launch.** A new library opens to a six-step assistant: welcome, where your music lives (leave files in place, or copy and organize them; then find music on this Mac, add a folder or connect to a server, with live counts), which output to use (every connected device, with the best one marked), sound (exclusive access, ReplayGain, and whether the volume keys follow Vespertine), extras (background quality checks, cover art, automatic updates), and a summary.
- **Only once.** It shows until you finish or skip it. Libraries that already have music never see it, and **Vespertine › Setup Assistant…** brings it back.
- **Calm with Reduce Motion.** Pages cross-fade and the background stays still when Reduce Motion is on.

### Remembered output
- **Your choice sticks.** The output you choose is remembered and used whenever it's connected, even when it wasn't there at launch.
- **A stand-in meanwhile.** Until it returns, Vespertine plays on a stand-in, set in **Settings › Playback › "When the chosen output isn't connected, play on"**: the best connected output (the default), the Mac's sound output, or nothing (wait for it). The best output is an external USB, Thunderbolt, PCI or FireWire device first, then the Mac's sound output, then built-in, then HDMI, Bluetooth and AirPlay; virtual devices only if nothing else is there.
- **Clear about it.** The output menu keeps your choice checked as NOT CONNECTED · USING the stand-in, and the inspector says "Waiting for …" instead of "Preparing output…". Playback moves back when the output is plugged in again.
- **Brief dropouts.** If the chosen output disappeared moments ago (AirPods reconnecting), Vespertine waits up to 10 seconds for it before using the stand-in. A dropout in the middle of a song still pauses and waits, as before.
- **A DAC on another port.** A DAC that comes back under a new identity (plugged into another USB port) is recognized and keeps its rate, DoP, receiver, Spatial Audio and EQ settings.

### Match 16-bit sources
- **New setting.** **Settings › Playback › Output › Match 16-bit sources**, off by default and available with exclusive access. When it's on, a 16-bit file goes to a DAC that has a 16-bit mode at that rate as 16-bit, instead of zero-padded to 24 or 32 bits. The samples are identical either way.
- **When it applies.** Only for 16-bit PCM at its own rate and channel count, on a device held exclusively (not the Mac's own speakers or headphone jack), with no digital volume, EQ, ReplayGain, Spatial Audio or downmix. DSD, DoP and bitstream playback are never affected.
- **The signal path says what happened.** A Match 16-bit sources step reads what the DAC accepted: sent as 16-bit, no 16-bit mode at that rate (sent as 24-bit, same samples), or the device kept its depth despite the request.
- **Other apps unaffected.** When matched playback ends, the device goes back to its full bit depth.

### Loopback test
- **Check Vespertine's own output path.** **Controls › Loopback Test…** (also in Settings › Playback) plays a test signal through the real decoder and engine to a virtual loopback device, records what comes back and compares it sample by sample. Choose a quick run (24-bit at 44.1 and 96 kHz, 16-bit padded, and a gapless pair) or a full run (every common rate from 44.1 to 384 kHz at 24-bit, 16-bit padded and matched, 32-bit integer, gapless and 16→24 pairs).
- **Diagnoses, not just pass or fail.** A failure names what went wrong: dropped or repeated frames, truncation, dither, a gain change, swapped or inverted channels, unlocked clocks, or a recording glitch in the test setup.
- **Results you can keep.** Copy Report puts a Markdown report on the clipboard. Results are saved per device, format, settings, macOS version and app version, and the inspector's signal path shows the playing format's last result as "Loopback (software check)".
- **Honest about its scope.** It checks Vespertine's software path only. It says nothing about a DAC and never feeds the BIT-PERFECT badge. It needs a virtual loopback device: the source tree's `scripts/install-loopback-device.sh` builds a dedicated "Vespertine Loopback" from BlackHole. Recording that device asks for microphone permission once; no microphone is ever recorded. See [LOOPBACK.md](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine/blob/main/docs/LOOPBACK.md).
- **From the command line.** `vespertine-probe loopback [--quick|--full] [--json] [--markdown <path>]` runs the same test unattended.

### Faster DSD
- **DSD CUE tracks start at once.** A track deep into a DSF or DSDIFF CUE album, and any seek in a long DSD file, used to read the file from the start up to that point: 20 seconds or more from a network share. Vespertine now jumps straight to the position, so DSD starts and seeks as quickly as FLAC. The DSD and converted PCM samples are identical to reading straight through.

### Fixed
- **Scrubbing.** The seek bar's thumb stays exactly under the pointer while you drag, instead of running ahead of it toward the end of the track. The volume sliders get the same fix.

### Also
- **The installer window** now carries a small Ukrainian flag and "Thank you for supporting Ukraine!" The [README](https://github.com/szeremeta1/Vespertine#readme) links to United24, Come Back Alive and Razom for Ukraine.
- **New screenshots, tour, trailer and site** for the current feature set.

### Known issues
- **Volume sync with exclusive access.** While Vespertine holds a DAC exclusively, macOS moves the Mac's sound output to another device, often the built-in speakers, and Vespertine copies the DAC's volume onto that output so the volume keys keep working. Other apps' sounds on that output then play at the DAC's level, which can be much louder than usual, and the DAC's own Mac-side level can drift below 100%. A fix is in progress. Until then, turning off exclusive access avoids it, or check the DAC's level in Audio MIDI Setup if bit-perfect playback matters.
- Some German and Portuguese labels are cut off, and a stray icon appears on the search page.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.11.2.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID (Alexander Szeremeta, `7WMQ9ZV6V8`), notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.

name: Vespertine 0.11.1
body:
**Album editions now share one card, and later tracks in DSD CUE albums play without the region-decoder crash.**

### Album editions
- **One card per album.** Recognized remasters, mono and stereo releases, SACDs and other tagged editions appear together in the library, artist, genre, source, recent and search views.
- **Choose the edition.** Open the album to select a release with Choose Edition or its edition card. Each release keeps its own tracks, artwork and format.
- **Page playback plays each album once.** Play, Shuffle and queue actions select one matching edition per album, including on filtered pages.
- **Music stays in place.** Grouping changes the presentation; it does not move, delete or retag your files.

### Fixed
- **DSD CUE playback.** CUE offsets are converted from the native DSD frame rate into the decoder's PCM or DoP frame rate before opening a track. Later tracks no longer use offsets beyond the decoder's end.
- **Invalid CUE regions.** An empty or out-of-range region returns a playback error instead of aborting the app. Final-track lengths remain clamped to the audio available.

### Install
Download **Vespertine-0.11.1.dmg**, or let Vespertine update itself. Requires macOS 14.4 or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID (Alexander Szeremeta, `7WMQ9ZV6V8`), notarized and stapled. Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask vespertine`.
